events.headline: Lamar Jackson (ankle) leaves Titans game at halftime and does not return; Minter has no update
events.detail: Jackson was hurt on the last offensive play of the first half when Jermaine Johnson landed on the back of his leg on a sack. He was 15 of 20 for 222 yards and two TDs plus 20 rushing yards at the break, with Baltimore up 24-7. Tyler Huntley played the second half. Jesse Minter said the team does not "know enough about it" yet. Zay Flowers was active despite his Questionable tag and caught 8 of 10 targets for 118 yards and a TD.
events.so_what: Wait for Monday's imaging before doing anything. If Jackson misses time, the konami rushing premium goes with him and Huntley is a deep streamer only; anyone rostering Jackson without a second QB should look at the wire Tuesday. Flowers' hamstring is no longer a concern.

events.headline: Saquon Barkley (hamstring) ruled out on his second carry vs. Rams; Tank Bigsby takes over
events.detail: Barkley was hurt on his second carry, 11:34 into the first quarter, after two carries for 8 yards, and was ruled out. Tank Bigsby replaced him. Philadelphia was already without DeVonta Smith, Dallas Goedert and Lane Johnson, and lost CB Quinyon Mitchell (knee) and Jonathan Greenard (ankle) during the game. The Rams won 24-20.
events.so_what: No diagnosis yet; treat Barkley as doubtful for Week 5 until the Eagles say otherwise. Bigsby is the priority Tuesday add for anyone needing RB help, as the early-down back behind a banged-up line. Hold Barkley: a hamstring is usually weeks, not a season.

events.headline: Ja'Marr Chase ruled out with a concussion vs. Jaguars; Tee Higgins goes 11-157
events.detail: Chase hit his head on the turf after a facemask tackle early in the second quarter and was declared out at halftime. Tee Higgins caught 11 of 16 targets for 157 yards in the loss to Jacksonville.
events.so_what: Chase enters the concussion protocol, which makes Week 5 uncertain; watch for a full practice by Friday before starting him. Higgins becomes Burrow's lead target if Chase sits and is a WR1-level start in that case.

events.headline: Kyle Monangai runs 30 times for 146 yards and two TDs as Bears beat Jets; leaves late with a thumb injury
events.detail: D'Andre Swift, cleared from a knee issue Friday, fumbled in the third quarter and finished with 15 carries for 58 yards while Monangai took over the lead role. Monangai exited late with a thumb injury; Ben Johnson said he is being evaluated. Tyson Bagent went 25 of 34 for 268 yards and an INT in a 23-12 win.
events.so_what: Monangai is no longer a handcuff: 30 carries and the goal-line work make him a FLEX start in a split with Swift, pending the thumb. Swift drops to a shakier RB2/FLEX. If he is still on your wire, he is the top RB add of the week.

events.headline: D.J. Moore aggravates shoulder vs. Patriots, downgraded to doubtful to return
events.detail: Moore hurt the same shoulder he injured in Week 2 diving for a sideline catch late in the second quarter, and was downgraded to doubtful at halftime. He had been limited in practice since Week 2 but had not missed a game. Buffalo lost 29-26.
events.so_what: A re-aggravation of a lingering injury is the kind that costs games. Check his Wednesday practice status before starting him in Week 5; keep a healthy FLEX on the bench as cover.

events.headline: Ladd McConkey (foot) active at Seattle; Derwin James inactive
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 2 item. McConkey is not on the Chargers inactive list after a limited Friday without routes. Derwin James (hamstring), Brenen Thompson (quad) and TE Charlie Kolar (forearm) are inactive.
events.so_what: He plays. A foot that kept him from running routes Friday is still a snap-count risk, so he is a FLEX rather than a locked WR2 in the 4:25 ET game.

events.headline: Mike Evans (ribs) active vs. Broncos after a pregame workout
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 2 item. Evans, a game-time decision after only side work Friday, is not on the 49ers inactive list. Inactive: DE Nick Bosa, RB Jordan James, QB Kurtis Rourke and four others.
events.so_what: He is active, but three days without team drills and a rib injury make his snap share the risk; treat him as a FLEX this week rather than a WR2.

events.headline: Kenyon Sadiq (back) active vs. Bears; Mason Taylor inactive
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 2 item. Sadiq, Questionable with a back injury, is not on the Jets' official inactive list. Inactive: RB Breece Hall, WR Adonai Mitchell, TE Mason Taylor, OG Dylan Parham, LB Kiko Mauigoa, CB Nahshon Wright and EDGE Kingsley Enagbare. Sadiq played 57.6% of snaps with a 7-105-1 line in Week 3 with Taylor out.
events.so_what: Start Sadiq as the streaming TE: active, with Taylor and Mitchell both out, he has the tight-end role to himself and an open share of the targets. Locks at the 1:00 ET kickoff.

source.label: The Jet Press, Jets Week 4 inactives, Oct. 4

events.headline: Tyjae Spears (ankle) active vs. Ravens; Tony Pollard cleared, Michael Carter inactive
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 2 item. Spears, Questionable after Robert Saleh said he had hurdles to clear, is not on the Titans' official inactive list. Inactive: RB Michael Carter, CB Jaylon Jones, OG Drew Moss, OT Brandon Crenshaw-Dickson, TE Kylen Granson and DT Jackie Marshall. Pollard had no designation and had 21 touches for 96 yards in Week 3.
events.so_what: Pollard stays a volume FLEX, but Spears being active takes back some of the passing-down work, so trim expectations a little. Spears himself is not a start in a split against Baltimore.

source.label: Yahoo Sports, Titans vs. Ravens inactives, Oct. 4

events.headline: DeVonta Smith inactive vs. Rams and unlikely for Week 5; Goedert, Brown, Lane Johnson also out
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 2 item. Smith (hamstring), Hollywood Brown, Dallas Goedert, LB Zack Baun and OTs Lane Johnson and Fred Johnson are on the Eagles' official inactive list. NFL Network's Mike Garafolo reports Smith is unlikely to return in Week 5 against Jacksonville. Dontayvion Wicks and rookie Makai Lemon take the receiver snaps, and Zach Ertz the extra tight-end work.
events.so_what: Bench all three, and plan on Smith missing Week 5 too. Wicks is the WR who absorbs volume and a deep FLEX this week; with two starting tackles out, temper expectations for the whole Eagles passing game. Wicks is the Tuesday FAAB target over Lemon.

events.headline: Terry McLaurin (hamstring) inactive for London vs. Colts; Daniels and White also out
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 3 item. McLaurin is on Washington's official inactive list along with Jayden Daniels (elbow), Rachaad White (shoulder) and WR Luke McCaffrey. Marcus Mariota starts. For Indianapolis, Keenan Allen (groin), WR Darius Slayton and RB DJ Giddens are inactive, with Josh Downs the top remaining Colts wideout. The game kicked off at 9:30 a.m. ET, so these lineups are already locked.
events.so_what: Nothing left to act on for this game. If McLaurin is still in a lineup it scores zero; there is no swap once London kicks off. Diggs was the right pivot as the first read for Mariota, and Antonio Williams a deep-league dart only.

source.label: Yahoo Sports, Colts vs. Commanders Week 4 inactives, Oct. 4

events.headline: Seahawks place Jadarian Price (chest) on injured reserve; Emanuel Wilson leads, Charbonnet window open
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 2 item. Seattle moved Price to IR on Saturday after he aggravated the Week 2 chest injury in Wednesday practice, so he misses at least four games and is eligible again in Week 8. He was the team's leading rusher (28 carries, 119 yards). Emanuel Wilson and George Holani handle the backfield; Zach Charbonnet's 21-day practice window is open and Mike Macdonald tied his activation to roster spots. The next four opponents are the Chargers, 49ers, Broncos and Chiefs.
events.so_what: Price is an IR stash for a month, not a drop, and he fits an IR slot. Wilson goes from one-week dart to the likely early-down back for several weeks, which makes him a real FLEX candidate on volume and TD equity until Charbonnet is activated. Watch Charbonnet's activation: once he is on the 53, this becomes a committee again.

events.headline: Justin Jefferson (ankle) out vs. Dolphins, "hopeful" to return Week 5 at New Orleans
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 2 item. Jefferson is out for Week 4 after not practicing all week. ESPN's Jeremy Fowler reported Saturday that he is hopeful to play in Week 5 against the Saints and the team does not view the ankle as a long-term problem. Kevin O'Connell has said Jefferson comes back only when he can "be himself."
events.so_what: Bench him this week and hold. "Hopeful" for Week 5 is a forecast, not a clearance; check Wednesday's practice report before planning around him. Jordan Addison gets the target bump for one week.

events.headline: Panthers place Xavier Legette (knee) on injured reserve; Jalen Coker (quad) still questionable vs. Lions
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 2 item. Carolina put Legette on IR Saturday, so he misses at least four more games. Coker remains Questionable for Sunday night after limited work Friday; Dave Canales said the team will keep evaluating him through the weekend. WR Ja'seem Reed was elevated from the practice squad as cover.
events.so_what: Legette is an IR stash at best. Coker is a Sunday-night late-swap risk with no later fallback, and the Reed elevation hints Carolina is preparing for him to sit; only start him if you can live with a zero.

events.headline: Caleb Williams (hamstring) out vs. Jets; Tyson Bagent expected to start over Case Keenum
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 2 item. Williams misses a second straight game with a Grade 2 hamstring strain. Ian Rapoport reported Bagent would likely start and The Athletic's Dan Wiederer confirmed it Saturday, after Bagent took most of the first-team reps this week. Keenum went 24 of 34 for 247 yards and two touchdowns in the Week 3 win over the Eagles. Ben Johnson has not announced it officially.
events.so_what: Bench Williams. Bagent is not a fantasy start in any of the three leagues. Bears receivers and backs keep their roles, but a backup making his first start since camp is a mild downgrade on their passing-game upside this week.

events.headline: Keenan Allen (groin) downgraded to out for London vs. Commanders
events.detail: The Colts ruled Allen out for Sunday morning's game in London after he was limited early in the week and could not practice Friday. Josh Downs and tight end Tyler Warren are the most likely beneficiaries of his targets.
events.so_what: Bench Allen; this is a 9:30 a.m. ET kickoff, so set lineups Saturday night. Downs moves up into FLEX range as the top remaining Colts wideout, and Warren's weekly floor at TE improves with one fewer target competitor.

events.headline: Keaton Mitchell cleared, off the Chargers injury report for Week 4
events.detail: Mitchell, seen in a walking boot after Thursday's practice with an ankle injury, is off the final report and good to go at Seattle.
events.so_what: The boot was not a sign of an absence. Use him in his usual role.

events.headline: Rachaad White (shoulder) ruled out vs. Colts after missing every practice
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 1 item. White did not practice all week and is out for Sunday's game in London. Jayden Daniels, G Sam Cosmi and S Nick Cross are also out.
events.so_what: Bench White. Washington's remaining backs split a Mariota-led offense; no single beneficiary is confirmed by the team, so this is not a FAAB signal on its own.

events.headline: Breece Hall (quad) ruled out vs. Bears; Braelon Allen and Isaiah Davis split the work
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 1 item. Hall is out. Braelon Allen and Isaiah Davis are expected to handle most of his carries, and returner Kene Nwangwu is set to debut after a back injury.
events.so_what: Bench Hall. Allen is the better RB2/FLEX bet of the two for this week; neither has the job alone, and with Hall week-to-week, Allen is the one to bid on Tuesday if you need RB depth.

events.headline: Jayden Daniels (elbow) ruled out for London; Marcus Mariota starts vs. Colts
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 1 item. Dan Quinn ruled Daniels out Friday despite limited practices. Mariota starts against Indianapolis in London.
events.so_what: Bench Daniels. Mariota is a desperation streamer at best; the London game kicks off before the rest of the slate, so Washington decisions lock first.

events.headline: Puka Nacua cleared to play at Philadelphia after a two-game absence; Terrance Ferguson to injured reserve
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 30 item. Nacua carries no designation for the Eagles. Sean McVay said he looked sharp in Thursday's heavy session but that the staff is still working through his snap count and conditioning. TE Terrance Ferguson (ankle) was placed on injured reserve and Colby Parkinson (knee, shoulder) is Questionable.
events.so_what: Start Nacua as a WR1 against an Eagles defense now missing Zack Baun; a capped snap share is the only risk. Davante Adams loses some target share back to him. Drop any Ferguson start.

source.label: ESPN (Sarah Barshop): Aaron Donald out, Puka Nacua to play vs. Eagles

events.headline: Chris Godwin cleared, off the final Bucs report vs. Packers; Baker Mayfield ruled out, Jalon Daniels starts
events.detail: Update to the Oct. 1 item. Godwin (ankle) was a full participant Thursday and Friday after a Wednesday DNP and carries no designation for Green Bay; Bucky Irving is also off the final report. Baker Mayfield (dislocated right thumb, no ligament damage) is ruled out, and undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels makes his first NFL start. Godwin has 10 catches for 111 yards through three games.
events.so_what: Godwin plays; the rookie quarterback is what caps him, so he is a low-ceiling FLEX this week rather than a lineup lock. Any Bucs pass-catcher takes the same haircut until Mayfield returns, which Todd Bowles has framed as at least three weeks.

events.headline: Nico Collins cleared, off the Texans final report for Week 4 vs. Cowboys
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 30 item. Collins (Grade 1 hamstring) got in a full Friday session and is not on Houston's final injury report after missing two games. Houston scored 23 points combined without him against 31 with him in the opener, and Dallas has one of the league's weakest pass defenses through three weeks. In Week 2 without him Dalton Schultz caught 12 of 14 targets for 140 yards.
events.so_what: Start him. If he plays a full share, Schultz goes back to a secondary option and Xavier Hutchinson loses most of his volume, so neither is a FLEX answer this week.

events.headline: Jaylen Warren runs 17 times for 93 yards as Steelers lose 27-24 at Cleveland with Rico Dowdle out
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 30 item. With Dowdle (toe) inactive, Warren handled the backfield again Thursday night: 17 carries for 93 yards. Aaron Rodgers threw for 299 yards, three TDs and two INTs; DK Metcalf caught five for 115. Cleveland won on Andre Szmyt's 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds left. The Steelers fall to 2-2.
events.so_what: Warren has now carried the load in both games Dowdle has missed, so he stays a RB/FLEX start for as long as Dowdle is out. Dowdle remains a bench hold until he practices; watch next week's report, since Pittsburgh has extra rest after a Thursday game.

events.headline: Jaylen Wright upgrades to full Dolphins practice Thursday; Hafley describes a split with Ollie Gordon
events.detail: Update to the Sept. 30 item. Wright (stinger, foot) went from limited Wednesday to full Thursday. Jeff Hafley said the work behind the departed De'Von Achane will be split between Wright and Ollie Gordon depending on the play. Gordon took every running back snap in Week 3 after Achane tore his ACL, with 17 carries for 41 yards and a touchdown.
events.so_what: A full practice makes the committee real for Sunday. Gordon still looks like the early-down and goal-line back, which is where the TD value is, but neither should be started as a locked RB2 until one of them wins the snaps in a game.
